submitted.rationale: Index 22 (Fe 0.585, Ni 0.259, V 0.156) gave the highest photocurrent of the three measured compositions: 9e-8 A under 2.06 eV illumination. The MEGNet gap for FeVO4 (HSE 2.75 eV, PBE 2.08 eV) suggests the vanadate absorbs weakly at this photon energy, so the Fe-rich, V-poor corner is favoured. The measurements agree: the Fe-rich spots beat the near-FeVO4 spot.

rejected.reason: Close to FeVO4 stoichiometry; measured 2e-8 A, consistent with the vanadate's wide gap.
Also Fe-rich but with more V; measured 7e-8 A, below index 22.

consultations.verdict: MEGNet HSE gap of 2.75 eV for mp-504509 (an Fe–V oxide phase) is above the 2.06 eV photon energy. So the vanadate-rich phases probably absorb 602 nm light poorly. Fe-rich compositions, where an Fe2O3-like phase with a gap near 2.1 eV dominates, are more likely to absorb. I rate this weak support for measuring the most Fe-rich candidate, index 22.

MACE puts FeVO4 (mp-504509) on the convex hull, so it should form in the film. Index 79 (Fe 0.34, V 0.48, low Ni) sits close to FeVO4 stoichiometry. FeVO4 is a known photoanode, but its predicted HSE gap of 2.75 eV is above the 2.06 eV photons, so absorption may be weak. I rate the stability result as moderate support: this is worth one measurement to test the vanadate region against the Fe-rich result.

The PBE gap for FeVO4 is 2.08 eV and the HSE gap is 2.75 eV, so the vanadate absorbs weakly at 2.06 eV. That fits the measurements: the vanadate-region spot (index 79) gave 2e-8 A and the Fe-rich spot (index 22) gave 9e-8 A. This supports spending the last measurement in the Fe-rich corner. Index 46 has Fe 0.58 like index 22, with less Ni.
